input.content:
import paraview.simple as ps

ps.LoadPlugin  # no-op ensure module import ok

N_STEPS = 3
files = [f"/workspace/cylinder/cylinder{i+1}.vti" for i in range(N_STEPS)]

readers = []
calcs = []
for i, fn in enumerate(files):
    r = ps.OpenDataFile(fn)
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=r)
    # combine u,v into a vector array 'vec' (for glyphing) and magnitude scalar (for tracking)
    calc_vec = ps.Calculator(Input=r)
    calc_vec.ResultArrayName = "vec"
    calc_vec.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_vec.Function = "u*iHat+v*jHat"

    calc_mag = ps.Calculator(Input=calc_vec)
    calc_mag.ResultArrayName = f"mag_t{i}"
    calc_mag.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# Keep only the magnitude array (drop u,v,vec) on each branch, then append into one dataset
passers = []
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    p = ps.PassArrays(Input=c)
    p.PointDataArrays = [f"mag_t{i}"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p)
    passers.append(p)

merged = ps.AppendAttributes(Input=passers)
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=merged)

# --- Track critical points across the 3 timesteps using TTK's partial-OT-based
# persistence-diagram matcher (TrackingFromFields: Wasserstein matching allows
# points to be matched to the diagonal, i.e. partial optimal transport between
# consecutive persistence diagrams).
tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=merged)
tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
tracking.Timesampling = 1
tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.0
tracking.pparameter = "2"
tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
tracking.Xweight = 1.0
tracking.Yweight = 1.0
tracking.Zweight = 0.0
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=tracking)

trackOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(tracking)
print("Tracking output type:", trackOut.GetClassName())
print("N points:", trackOut.GetNumberOfPoints(), "N cells:", trackOut.GetNumberOfCells())

# ---------------- Visualization ----------------
view = ps.CreateRenderView()
view.ViewSize = [1200, 900]
view.OrientationAxesVisibility = 0
view.Background = [1, 1, 1]

# Show vector field glyphs for each timestep, offset in Z to separate them visually
colors = [[0.2, 0.4, 0.9], [0.2, 0.8, 0.3], [0.9, 0.3, 0.2]]
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    transform = ps.Transform(Input=c)
    transform.Transform = "Transform"

import paraview.simple as ps

ps.LoadPlugin  # no-op ensure module import ok

N_STEPS = 3
files = [f"/workspace/cylinder/cylinder{i+1}.vti" for i in range(N_STEPS)]

readers = []
calcs = []
for i, fn in enumerate(files):
    r = ps.OpenDataFile(fn)
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=r)
    # combine u,v into a vector array 'vec' (for glyphing) and magnitude scalar (for tracking)
    calc_vec = ps.Calculator(Input=r)
    calc_vec.ResultArrayName = "vec"
    calc_vec.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_vec.Function = "u*iHat+v*jHat"

    calc_mag = ps.Calculator(Input=calc_vec)
    calc_mag.ResultArrayName = f"mag_t{i}"
    calc_mag.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# Keep only the magnitude array (drop u,v,vec) on each branch, then append into one dataset
passers = []
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    p = ps.PassArrays(Input=c)
    p.PointDataArrays = [f"mag_t{i}"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p)
    passers.append(p)

merged = ps.AppendAttributes(Input=passers)
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=merged)

# --- Track critical points across the 3 timesteps using TTK's partial-OT-based
# persistence-diagram matcher (TrackingFromFields: Wasserstein matching allows
# points to be matched to the diagonal, i.e. partial optimal transport between
# consecutive persistence diagrams).
tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=merged)
tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
tracking.Timesampling = 1
tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.05
tracking.pparameter = "2"
tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
tracking.Xweight = 1.0
tracking.Yweight = 1.0
tracking.Zweight = 0.0
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=tracking)

trackOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(tracking)
print("Tracking output type:", trackOut.GetClassName())
print("N points:", trackOut.GetNumberOfPoints(), "N cells:", trackOut.GetNumberOfCells())

# ---------------- Visualization ----------------
view = ps.CreateRenderView()
view.ViewSize = [1200, 900]
view.OrientationAxesVisibility = 0
view.Background = [1, 1, 1]
view.UseColorPaletteForBackground = 0

# Show vector field glyphs for each timestep, offset in Z to separate them visually
colors = [[0.2, 0.4, 0.9], [0.2, 0.8, 0.3], [0.9, 0.3, 0.2]]
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    transform = ps.Transform(Input=c)
    transform.Transform = "Transform"
    transform.Transform.Translate = [0.0, 0.0, i * 50.0]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=transform)

    glyph = ps.Glyph(Input=transform, GlyphType="2D Glyph")
    glyph.GlyphType.GlyphType = "Arrow"
    glyph.OrientationArray = ["POINTS", "vec"]
    glyph.ScaleArray = ["POINTS", "vec"]
    glyph.ScaleFactor = 100.0
    glyph.GlyphMode = "Every Nth Point"
    glyph.Stride = 137
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=glyph)
    gOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(glyph)
    print(f"glyph {i} points:", gOut.GetNumberOfPoints())

    disp = ps.Show(glyph, view)
    disp.Representation = "Surface"
    disp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
    disp.AmbientColor = colors[i]
    disp.DiffuseColor = colors[i]
    disp.Opacity = 0.9

# Translate tracking output the same way is not needed since it already lives
# in field domain coords across "time" via ZTranslation-based embedding used
# internally; instead we translate a copy per critical-point subset for display
# alignment with the offset glyphs above.
trans_track = ps.Transform(Input=tracking)
trans_track.Transform = "Transform"
trans_track.Transform.Scale = [1.0, 1.0, 50.0]
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=trans_track)

tdisp = ps.Show(trans_track, view)
tdisp.Representation = "Surface"
tdisp.LineWidth = 4.0
tdisp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
tdisp.AmbientColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
tdisp.DiffuseColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

pdisp = ps.Show(trans_track, view)
pdisp.Representation = "Points"
pdisp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
pdisp.PointSize = 10.0
pdisp.RenderPointsAsSpheres = 1
pdisp.AmbientColor = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0]
pdisp.DiffuseColor = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0]

ps.ResetCamera(view)
view.CameraPosition = [75, -1400, 500]
view.CameraFocalPoint = [75, 225, 50]
view.CameraViewUp = [0, 0, 1]
view.CameraParallelProjection = 0

ps.Render(view)
ps.SaveScreenshot("/workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png", view, ImageResolution=[1600, 1200])

import paraview.simple as ps

ps.LoadPlugin  # no-op ensure module import ok

N_STEPS = 3
files = [f"/workspace/cylinder/cylinder{i+1}.vti" for i in range(N_STEPS)]

readers = []
calcs = []
for i, fn in enumerate(files):
    r = ps.OpenDataFile(fn)
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=r)
    # combine u,v into a vector array 'vec' (for glyphing) and magnitude scalar (for tracking)
    calc_vec = ps.Calculator(Input=r)
    calc_vec.ResultArrayName = "vec"
    calc_vec.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_vec.Function = "u*iHat+v*jHat"

    calc_mag = ps.Calculator(Input=calc_vec)
    calc_mag.ResultArrayName = f"mag_t{i}"
    calc_mag.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# Keep only the magnitude array (drop u,v,vec) on each branch, then append into one dataset
passers = []
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    p = ps.PassArrays(Input=c)
    p.PointDataArrays = [f"mag_t{i}"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p)
    passers.append(p)

merged = ps.AppendAttributes(Input=passers)
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=merged)

# --- Track critical points across the 3 timesteps using TTK's partial-OT-based
# persistence-diagram matcher (TrackingFromFields: Wasserstein matching allows
# points to be matched to the diagonal, i.e. partial optimal transport between
# consecutive persistence diagrams).
tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=merged)
tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
tracking.Timesampling = 1
tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.15
tracking.pparameter = "2"
tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
tracking.Xweight = 1.0
tracking.Yweight = 1.0
tracking.Zweight = 0.0
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=tracking)

trackOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(tracking)
print("Tracking output type:", trackOut.GetClassName())
print("N points:", trackOut.GetNumberOfPoints(), "N cells:", trackOut.GetNumberOfCells())

# ---------------- Visualization ----------------
view = ps.CreateRenderView()
view.ViewSize = [1200, 900]
view.OrientationAxesVisibility = 0
view.Background = [1, 1, 1]
view.UseColorPaletteForBackground = 0

# Show vector field glyphs for each timestep, offset in Z to separate them visually
colors = [[0.2, 0.4, 0.9], [0.2, 0.8, 0.3], [0.9, 0.3, 0.2]]
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    transform = ps.Transform(Input=c)
    transform.Transform = "Transform"
    transform.Transform.Translate = [0.0, 0.0, i * 50.0]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=transform)

    glyph = ps.Glyph(Input=transform, GlyphType="2D Glyph")
    glyph.GlyphType.GlyphType = "Arrow"
    glyph.OrientationArray = ["POINTS", "vec"]
    glyph.ScaleArray = ["POINTS", "vec"]
    glyph.ScaleFactor = 100.0
    glyph.GlyphMode = "Every Nth Point"
    glyph.Stride = 137
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=glyph)
    gOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(glyph)
    print(f"glyph {i} points:", gOut.GetNumberOfPoints())

    disp = ps.Show(glyph, view)
    disp.Representation = "Surface"
    disp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
    disp.AmbientColor = colors[i]
    disp.DiffuseColor = colors[i]
    disp.Opacity = 0.9

# Translate tracking output the same way is not needed since it already lives
# in field domain coords across "time" via ZTranslation-based embedding used
# internally; instead we translate a copy per critical-point subset for display
# alignment with the offset glyphs above.
trans_track = ps.Calculator(Input=tracking)
trans_track.CoordinateResults = 1
trans_track.Function = "coordsX*iHat + coordsY*jHat + (TimeStep*50)*kHat"
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=trans_track)

tdisp = ps.Show(trans_track, view)
tdisp.Representation = "Surface"
tdisp.LineWidth = 4.0
tdisp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
tdisp.AmbientColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
tdisp.DiffuseColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

pdisp = ps.Show(trans_track, view)
pdisp.Representation = "Points"
pdisp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
pdisp.PointSize = 7.0
pdisp.RenderPointsAsSpheres = 1
pdisp.AmbientColor = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0]
pdisp.DiffuseColor = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0]

ps.ResetCamera(view)
cam = ps.GetActiveCamera(view)
cam.Azimuth(35)
cam.Elevation(25)
ps.ResetCamera(view)
cam.Zoom(1.3)

ps.Render(view)
ps.SaveScreenshot("/workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png", view, ImageResolution=[1600, 1200])
print("Saved /workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png")

ps.SaveData("/workspace/cylinder_tracking.vtu", proxy=tracking)
print("Saved /workspace/cylinder_tracking.vtu")

import paraview.simple as ps

ps.LoadPlugin  # no-op ensure module import ok

N_STEPS = 3
files = [f"/workspace/cylinder/cylinder{i+1}.vti" for i in range(N_STEPS)]

readers = []
calcs = []
for i, fn in enumerate(files):
    r = ps.OpenDataFile(fn)
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=r)
    # combine u,v into a vector array 'vec' (for glyphing) and magnitude scalar (for tracking)
    calc_vec = ps.Calculator(Input=r)
    calc_vec.ResultArrayName = "vec"
    calc_vec.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_vec.Function = "u*iHat+v*jHat"

    calc_mag = ps.Calculator(Input=calc_vec)
    calc_mag.ResultArrayName = f"mag_t{i}"
    calc_mag.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# Keep only the magnitude array (drop u,v,vec) on each branch, then append into one dataset
passers = []
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    p = ps.PassArrays(Input=c)
    p.PointDataArrays = [f"mag_t{i}"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p)
    passers.append(p)

merged = ps.AppendAttributes(Input=passers)
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=merged)

# --- Track critical points across the 3 timesteps using TTK's partial-OT-based
# persistence-diagram matcher (TrackingFromFields: Wasserstein matching allows
# points to be matched to the diagonal, i.e. partial optimal transport between
# consecutive persistence diagrams).
tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=merged)
tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
tracking.Timesampling = 1
tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.15
tracking.pparameter = "2"
tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
tracking.Xweight = 1.0
tracking.Yweight = 1.0
tracking.Zweight = 0.0
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=tracking)

trackOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(tracking)
print("Tracking output type:", trackOut.GetClassName())
print("N points:", trackOut.GetNumberOfPoints(), "N cells:", trackOut.GetNumberOfCells())

# ---------------- Visualization ----------------
view = ps.CreateRenderView()
view.ViewSize = [1200, 900]
view.OrientationAxesVisibility = 0
view.Background = [1, 1, 1]
view.UseColorPaletteForBackground = 0

# Show vector field glyphs for each timestep, offset in Z to separate them visually
colors = [[0.2, 0.4, 0.9], [0.2, 0.8, 0.3], [0.9, 0.3, 0.2]]
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    transform = ps.Transform(Input=c)
    transform.Transform = "Transform"
    transform.Transform.Translate = [0.0, 0.0, i * 180.0]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=transform)

    glyph = ps.Glyph(Input=transform, GlyphType="2D Glyph")
    glyph.GlyphType.GlyphType = "Arrow"
    glyph.OrientationArray = ["POINTS", "vec"]
    glyph.ScaleArray = ["POINTS", "vec"]
    glyph.ScaleFactor = 70.0
    glyph.GlyphMode = "Every Nth Point"
    glyph.Stride = 211
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=glyph)
    gOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(glyph)
    print(f"glyph {i} points:", gOut.GetNumberOfPoints())

    disp = ps.Show(glyph, view)
    disp.Representation = "Surface"
    disp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
    disp.AmbientColor = colors[i]
    disp.DiffuseColor = colors[i]
    disp.Opacity = 0.9

# Translate tracking output the same way is not needed since it already lives
# in field domain coords across "time" via ZTranslation-based embedding used
# internally; instead we translate a copy per critical-point subset for display
# alignment with the offset glyphs above.
trans_track = ps.Calculator(Input=tracking)
trans_track.CoordinateResults = 1
trans_track.Function = "coordsX*iHat + coordsY*jHat + (TimeStep*180)*kHat"
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=trans_track)

tdisp = ps.Show(trans_track, view)
tdisp.Representation = "Surface"
tdisp.LineWidth = 4.0
tdisp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
tdisp.AmbientColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
tdisp.DiffuseColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

pdisp = ps.Show(trans_track, view)
pdisp.Representation = "Points"
pdisp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
pdisp.PointSize = 7.0
pdisp.RenderPointsAsSpheres = 1
pdisp.AmbientColor = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0]
pdisp.DiffuseColor = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0]

ps.ResetCamera(view)
cam = view.GetActiveCamera()
cam.Azimuth(25)
cam.Elevation(15)
ps.ResetCamera(view)

ps.Render(view)
ps.SaveScreenshot("/workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png", view, ImageResolution=[1600, 1200])
print("Saved /workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png")

ps.SaveData("/workspace/cylinder_tracking.vtu", proxy=tracking)
print("Saved /workspace/cylinder_tracking.vtu")

import paraview.simple as ps

N_STEPS = 3
files = [f"/workspace/cylinder/cylinder{i+1}.vti" for i in range(N_STEPS)]

readers = []
calcs = []
for i, fn in enumerate(files):
    r = ps.OpenDataFile(fn)
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=r)
    # combine u,v into a vector array 'vec' (for glyphing) and magnitude scalar (for tracking)
    calc_vec = ps.Calculator(Input=r)
    calc_vec.ResultArrayName = "vec"
    calc_vec.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_vec.Function = "u*iHat+v*jHat"

    calc_mag = ps.Calculator(Input=calc_vec)
    calc_mag.ResultArrayName = f"mag_t{i}"
    calc_mag.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# Keep only the magnitude array (drop u,v,vec) on each branch, then append into one dataset
passers = []
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    p = ps.PassArrays(Input=c)
    p.PointDataArrays = [f"mag_t{i}"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p)
    passers.append(p)

merged = ps.AppendAttributes(Input=passers)
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=merged)

# --- Track critical points across the 3 timesteps using TTK's partial-OT-based
# persistence-diagram matcher (TrackingFromFields: Wasserstein matching allows
# points to be matched to the diagonal, i.e. partial optimal transport between
# consecutive persistence diagrams -- critical points can be born/die between
# steps instead of forcing a full bijection).
tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=merged)
tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
tracking.Timesampling = 1
tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.15
tracking.pparameter = "2"
tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
tracking.Xweight = 1.0
tracking.Yweight = 1.0
tracking.Zweight = 0.0
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=tracking)

trackOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(tracking)
print("Tracking output type:", trackOut.GetClassName())
print("N points:", trackOut.GetNumberOfPoints(), "N cells:", trackOut.GetNumberOfCells())

# The raw output labels each edge endpoint with a LOCAL TimeStep (0/1) relative
# to its own consecutive-pair match, not a global time index, and edges from
# different (t,t+1) pairs are simply concatenated. Recover the true global
# timestep of every point by nearest-neighbor matching against independently
# computed per-timestep critical point locations, so we can place/color things
# correctly by actual time.
Z_GAP = 180.0


def compute_critical_points(calc_proxy, array_name):
    cp = ps.TTKScalarFieldCriticalPoints(Input=calc_proxy)
    cp.ScalarField = ["POINTS", array_name]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=cp)
    out = ps.servermanager.Fetch(cp)
    import vtk.util.numpy_support as ns
    import numpy as np
    if out.GetNumberOfPoints() == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 2))
    return ns.vtk_to_numpy(out.GetPoints().GetData())[:, :2].astype(float)


cp_sets = [compute_critical_points(c, f"mag_t{i}") for i, c in enumerate(calcs)]

reassign = ps.ProgrammableFilter(Input=tracking)
reassign.Script = f"""
import numpy as np
from vtkmodules.util import numpy_support as ns

Z_GAP = {Z_GAP}
cp_sets = {[s.tolist() for s in cp_sets]!r}
cp_sets = [np.array(s) for s in cp_sets]

inp = self.GetInputDataObject(0, 0)
out = self.GetOutputDataObject(0)
out.ShallowCopy(inp)

pts = ns.vtk_to_numpy(inp.GetPoints().GetData())[:, :2]
real_t = np.full(pts.shape[0], -1, dtype=np.int32)
for i, pt in enumerate(pts):
    best_t, best_d = -1, 1e18
    for t, cps in enumerate(cp_sets):
        if len(cps) == 0:
            continue
        d = np.min(np.sum((cps - pt) ** 2, axis=1))
        if d < best_d:
            best_d, best_t = d, t
    real_t[i] = best_t

new_pts = np.column_stack([pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1], real_t.astype(float) * Z_GAP])
vtk_pts = ns.numpy_to_vtk(new_pts, deep=True)
out.GetPoints().SetData(vtk_pts)

rt_arr = ns.numpy_to_vtk(real_t, deep=True)
rt_arr.SetName("RealTimeStep")
out.GetPointData().AddArray(rt_arr)
"""
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=reassign)

rtOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(reassign)
import vtk.util.numpy_support as ns2
rt = ns2.vtk_to_numpy(rtOut.GetPointData().GetArray("RealTimeStep"))
print("Recovered real timestep histogram:", {int(t): int((rt == t).sum()) for t in sorted(set(rt.tolist()))})

# ---------------- Visualization ----------------
view = ps.CreateRenderView()
view.ViewSize = [1600, 1200]
view.OrientationAxesVisibility = 0
view.Background = [1, 1, 1]
view.UseColorPaletteForBackground = 0

# Show vector field glyphs for each timestep, offset in Z to separate them visually
colors = [[0.2, 0.4, 0.9], [0.2, 0.8, 0.3], [0.9, 0.3, 0.2]]
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    transform = ps.Transform(Input=c)
    transform.Transform = "Transform"
    transform.Transform.Translate = [0.0, 0.0, i * Z_GAP]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=transform)

    glyph = ps.Glyph(Input=transform, GlyphType="Arrow")
    glyph.OrientationArray = ["POINTS", "vec"]
    glyph.ScaleArray = ["POINTS", "vec"]
    glyph.ScaleFactor = 70.0
    glyph.GlyphMode = "Every Nth Point"
    glyph.Stride = 211
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=glyph)

    disp = ps.Show(glyph, view)
    disp.Representation = "Surface"
    disp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
    disp.AmbientColor = colors[i]
    disp.DiffuseColor = colors[i]
    disp.Opacity = 0.85

tdisp = ps.Show(reassign, view)
tdisp.Representation = "Surface"
tdisp.LineWidth = 4.0
tdisp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
tdisp.AmbientColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
tdisp.DiffuseColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

pdisp = ps.Show(reassign, view)
pdisp.Representation = "Points"
pdisp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
pdisp.PointSize = 7.0
pdisp.RenderPointsAsSpheres = 1
pdisp.AmbientColor = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0]
pdisp.DiffuseColor = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0]

ps.ResetCamera(view)
cam = view.GetActiveCamera()
cam.Azimuth(25)
cam.Elevation(15)
ps.ResetCamera(view)

ps.Render(view)
ps.SaveScreenshot("/workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png", view, ImageResolution=[1600, 1200])
print("Saved /workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png")

ps.SaveData("/workspace/cylinder_tracking.vtu", proxy=reassign)
print("Saved /workspace/cylinder_tracking.vtu")

import paraview.simple as ps

ps.LoadPlugin  # no-op ensure module import ok

N_STEPS = 3
files = [f"/workspace/cylinder/cylinder{i+1}.vti" for i in range(N_STEPS)]

readers = []
calcs = []
for i, fn in enumerate(files):
    r = ps.OpenDataFile(fn)
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=r)
    # combine u,v into a vector array 'vec' (for glyphing) and magnitude scalar (for tracking)
    calc_vec = ps.Calculator(Input=r)
    calc_vec.ResultArrayName = "vec"
    calc_vec.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_vec.Function = "u*iHat+v*jHat"

    calc_mag = ps.Calculator(Input=calc_vec)
    calc_mag.ResultArrayName = f"mag_t{i}"
    calc_mag.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# Keep only the magnitude array (drop u,v,vec) on each branch, then append into one dataset
passers = []
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    p = ps.PassArrays(Input=c)
    p.PointDataArrays = [f"mag_t{i}"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p)
    passers.append(p)

merged = ps.AppendAttributes(Input=passers)
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=merged)

# --- Track critical points across the 3 timesteps using TTK's partial-OT-based
# persistence-diagram matcher (TrackingFromFields: Wasserstein matching allows
# points to be matched to the diagonal, i.e. partial optimal transport between
# consecutive persistence diagrams).
tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=merged)
tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
tracking.Timesampling = 1
tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.15
tracking.pparameter = "2"
tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
tracking.Xweight = 1.0
tracking.Yweight = 1.0
tracking.Zweight = 0.0
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=tracking)

trackOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(tracking)
print("Tracking output type:", trackOut.GetClassName())
print("N points:", trackOut.GetNumberOfPoints(), "N cells:", trackOut.GetNumberOfCells())

# ---------------- Visualization ----------------
view = ps.CreateRenderView()
view.ViewSize = [1200, 900]
view.OrientationAxesVisibility = 0
view.Background = [1, 1, 1]
view.UseColorPaletteForBackground = 0

# Show vector field glyphs for each timestep, offset in Z to separate them visually
colors = [[0.2, 0.4, 0.9], [0.2, 0.8, 0.3], [0.9, 0.3, 0.2]]
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    transform = ps.Transform(Input=c)
    transform.Transform = "Transform"
    transform.Transform.Translate = [0.0, 0.0, i * 180.0]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=transform)

    glyph = ps.Glyph(Input=transform, GlyphType="2D Glyph")
    glyph.GlyphType.GlyphType = "Arrow"
    glyph.OrientationArray = ["POINTS", "vec"]
    glyph.ScaleArray = ["POINTS", "vec"]
    glyph.ScaleFactor = 70.0
    glyph.GlyphMode = "Every Nth Point"
    glyph.Stride = 211
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=glyph)
    gOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(glyph)
    print(f"glyph {i} points:", gOut.GetNumberOfPoints())

    disp = ps.Show(glyph, view)
    disp.Representation = "Surface"
    disp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
    disp.AmbientColor = colors[i]
    disp.DiffuseColor = colors[i]
    disp.Opacity = 0.9

# Translate tracking output the same way is not needed since it already lives
# in field domain coords across "time" via ZTranslation-based embedding used
# internally; instead we translate a copy per critical-point subset for display
# alignment with the offset glyphs above.
trans_track = ps.Calculator(Input=tracking)
trans_track.CoordinateResults = 1
trans_track.Function = "coordsX*iHat + coordsY*jHat + (TimeStep*180)*kHat"
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=trans_track)

tdisp = ps.Show(trans_track, view)
tdisp.Representation = "Surface"
tdisp.LineWidth = 4.0
tdisp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
tdisp.AmbientColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
tdisp.DiffuseColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

pdisp = ps.Show(trans_track, view)
pdisp.Representation = "Points"
pdisp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
pdisp.PointSize = 7.0
pdisp.RenderPointsAsSpheres = 1
pdisp.AmbientColor = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0]
pdisp.DiffuseColor = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0]

ps.ResetCamera(view)
cam = view.GetActiveCamera()
cam.Azimuth(25)
cam.Elevation(15)
ps.ResetCamera(view)

ps.Render(view)
ps.SaveScreenshot("/workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png", view, ImageResolution=[1600, 1200])
print("Saved /workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png")

ps.SaveData("/workspace/cylinder_tracking.vtu", proxy=tracking)
print("Saved /workspace/cylinder_tracking.vtu")

import paraview.simple as ps

N_STEPS = 3
files = [f"/workspace/cylinder/cylinder{i+1}.vti" for i in range(N_STEPS)]

readers = []
calcs = []
for i, fn in enumerate(files):
    r = ps.OpenDataFile(fn)
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=r)
    # combine u,v into a vector array 'vec' (for glyphing) and magnitude scalar (for tracking)
    calc_vec = ps.Calculator(Input=r)
    calc_vec.ResultArrayName = "vec"
    calc_vec.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_vec.Function = "u*iHat+v*jHat"

    calc_mag = ps.Calculator(Input=calc_vec)
    calc_mag.ResultArrayName = f"mag_t{i}"
    calc_mag.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# Keep only the magnitude array (drop u,v,vec) on each branch, then append into one dataset
passers = []
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    p = ps.PassArrays(Input=c)
    p.PointDataArrays = [f"mag_t{i}"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p)
    passers.append(p)

merged = ps.AppendAttributes(Input=passers)
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=merged)

# --- Track critical points across the 3 timesteps using TTK's partial-OT-based
# persistence-diagram matcher (TrackingFromFields: Wasserstein matching allows
# points to be matched to the diagonal, i.e. partial optimal transport between
# consecutive persistence diagrams -- critical points can be born/die between
# steps instead of forcing a full bijection).
tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=merged)
tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
tracking.Timesampling = 1
tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.15
tracking.pparameter = "2"
tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
tracking.Xweight = 1.0
tracking.Yweight = 1.0
tracking.Zweight = 0.0
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=tracking)

trackOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(tracking)
print("Tracking output type:", trackOut.GetClassName())
print("N points:", trackOut.GetNumberOfPoints(), "N cells:", trackOut.GetNumberOfCells())

# The raw output labels each edge endpoint with a LOCAL TimeStep (0/1) relative
# to its own consecutive-pair match, not a global time index, and edges from
# different (t,t+1) pairs are simply concatenated. Recover the true global
# timestep of every point by nearest-neighbor matching against independently
# computed per-timestep critical point locations, so we can place/color things
# correctly by actual time.
Z_GAP = 180.0


def compute_critical_points(calc_proxy, array_name):
    cp = ps.TTKScalarFieldCriticalPoints(Input=calc_proxy)
    cp.ScalarField = ["POINTS", array_name]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=cp)
    out = ps.servermanager.Fetch(cp)
    import vtk.util.numpy_support as ns
    import numpy as np
    if out.GetNumberOfPoints() == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 2))
    return ns.vtk_to_numpy(out.GetPoints().GetData())[:, :2].astype(float)


cp_sets = [compute_critical_points(c, f"mag_t{i}") for i, c in enumerate(calcs)]

inp = self.GetInputDataObject(0, 0)
out = self.GetOutputDataObject(0)
out.ShallowCopy(inp)

pts = ns.vtk_to_numpy(inp.GetPoints().GetData())[:, :2]
real_t = np.full(pts.shape[0], -1, dtype=np.int32)
for i, pt in enumerate(pts):
    best_t, best_d = -1, 1e18
    for t, cps in enumerate(cp_sets):
        if len(cps) == 0:
            continue
        d = np.min(np.sum((cps - pt) ** 2, axis=1))
        if d < best_d:
            best_d, best_t = d, t

new_pts = np.column_stack([pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1], real_t.astype(float) * Z_GAP])

ps.SaveScreenshot("/workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png", view, ImageResolution=[1600, 1200])
print("Saved /workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png")

import paraview.simple as ps

N_STEPS = 3
files = [f"/workspace/cylinder/cylinder{i+1}.vti" for i in range(N_STEPS)]

readers = []
calcs = []
for i, fn in enumerate(files):
    r = ps.OpenDataFile(fn)
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=r)
    # combine u,v into a vector array 'vec' (for glyphing) and magnitude scalar (for tracking)
    calc_vec = ps.Calculator(Input=r)
    calc_vec.ResultArrayName = "vec"
    calc_vec.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_vec.Function = "u*iHat+v*jHat"

    calc_mag = ps.Calculator(Input=calc_vec)
    calc_mag.ResultArrayName = f"mag_t{i}"
    calc_mag.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# Keep only the magnitude array (drop u,v,vec) on each branch, then append into one dataset
passers = []
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    p = ps.PassArrays(Input=c)
    p.PointDataArrays = [f"mag_t{i}"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p)
    passers.append(p)

merged = ps.AppendAttributes(Input=passers)
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=merged)

# --- Track critical points across the 3 timesteps using TTK's partial-OT-based
# persistence-diagram matcher (TrackingFromFields: Wasserstein matching allows
# points to be matched to the diagonal, i.e. partial optimal transport between
# consecutive persistence diagrams -- critical points can be born/die between
# steps instead of forcing a full bijection).
tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=merged)
tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
tracking.Timesampling = 1
tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.15
tracking.pparameter = "2"
tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
tracking.Xweight = 1.0
tracking.Yweight = 1.0
tracking.Zweight = 0.0
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=tracking)

trackOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(tracking)
print("Tracking output type:", trackOut.GetClassName())
print("N points:", trackOut.GetNumberOfPoints(), "N cells:", trackOut.GetNumberOfCells())

# The raw output labels each edge endpoint with a LOCAL TimeStep (0/1) relative
# to its own consecutive-pair match, not a global time index, and edges from
# different (t,t+1) pairs are simply concatenated. Recover the true global
# timestep of every point by nearest-neighbor matching against independently
# computed per-timestep critical point locations, so we can place/color things
# correctly by actual time.
Z_GAP = 180.0


def compute_critical_points(calc_proxy, array_name):
    cp = ps.TTKScalarFieldCriticalPoints(Input=calc_proxy)
    cp.ScalarField = ["POINTS", array_name]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=cp)
    out = ps.servermanager.Fetch(cp)
    import vtk.util.numpy_support as ns
    import numpy as np
    if out.GetNumberOfPoints() == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 2))
    return ns.vtk_to_numpy(out.GetPoints().GetData())[:, :2].astype(float)


cp_sets = [compute_critical_points(c, f"mag_t{i}") for i, c in enumerate(calcs)]

import numpy as np
from vtkmodules.util import numpy_support as ns

pts = ns.vtk_to_numpy(trackOut.GetPoints().GetData())[:, :2]
real_t = np.full(pts.shape[0], -1, dtype=np.int32)
for i, pt in enumerate(pts):
    best_t, best_d = -1, 1e18
    for t, cps in enumerate(cp_sets):
        if len(cps) == 0:
            continue
        d = np.min(np.sum((cps - pt) ** 2, axis=1))
        if d < best_d:
            best_d, best_t = d, t
    real_t[i] = best_t

new_pts = np.column_stack([pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1], real_t.astype(float) * Z_GAP])
modified = trackOut.NewInstance()
modified.ShallowCopy(trackOut)
vtk_pts_arr = ns.numpy_to_vtk(new_pts, deep=True)
new_vtk_points = modified.GetPoints().NewInstance()
new_vtk_points.SetData(vtk_pts_arr)
modified.SetPoints(new_vtk_points)

rt_arr = ns.numpy_to_vtk(real_t, deep=True)
rt_arr.SetName("RealTimeStep")
modified.GetPointData().AddArray(rt_arr)

print("Recovered real timestep histogram:", {int(t): int((real_t == t).sum()) for t in sorted(set(real_t.tolist()))})

reassign = ps.TrivialProducer()
reassign.GetClientSideObject().SetOutput(modified)
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=reassign)

# ---------------- Visualization ----------------
view = ps.CreateRenderView()
view.ViewSize = [1600, 1200]
view.OrientationAxesVisibility = 0
view.Background = [1, 1, 1]
view.UseColorPaletteForBackground = 0

# Show vector field glyphs for each timestep, offset in Z to separate them visually
colors = [[0.2, 0.4, 0.9], [0.2, 0.8, 0.3], [0.9, 0.3, 0.2]]
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    transform = ps.Transform(Input=c)
    transform.Transform = "Transform"
    transform.Transform.Translate = [0.0, 0.0, i * Z_GAP]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=transform)

    glyph = ps.Glyph(Input=transform, GlyphType="Arrow")
    glyph.OrientationArray = ["POINTS", "vec"]
    glyph.ScaleArray = ["POINTS", "vec"]
    glyph.ScaleFactor = 70.0
    glyph.GlyphMode = "Every Nth Point"
    glyph.Stride = 211
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=glyph)

    disp = ps.Show(glyph, view)
    disp.Representation = "Surface"
    disp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
    disp.AmbientColor = colors[i]
    disp.DiffuseColor = colors[i]
    disp.Opacity = 0.85

tdisp = ps.Show(reassign, view)
tdisp.Representation = "Surface"
tdisp.LineWidth = 4.0
tdisp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
tdisp.AmbientColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
tdisp.DiffuseColor = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

pdisp = ps.Show(reassign, view)
pdisp.Representation = "Points"
pdisp.ColorArrayName = ["POINTS", ""]
pdisp.PointSize = 7.0
pdisp.RenderPointsAsSpheres = 1
pdisp.AmbientColor = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0]
pdisp.DiffuseColor = [1.0, 0.6, 0.0]

ps.ResetCamera(view)
cam = view.GetActiveCamera()
cam.Azimuth(25)
cam.Elevation(15)
ps.ResetCamera(view)

ps.Render(view)
ps.SaveScreenshot("/workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png", view, ImageResolution=[1600, 1200])
print("Saved /workspace/cylinder_tracked_critical_points.png")

ps.SaveData("/workspace/cylinder_tracking.vtu", proxy=reassign)
print("Saved /workspace/cylinder_tracking.vtu")

    calc_mag.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# --- Track critical points using TTK's partial-OT persistence-diagram matcher
# (TrackingFromFields: sparse-Munkres Wasserstein matching lets a critical
# point be matched to the diagonal, i.e. born/killed, rather than forcing a
# full bijection between consecutive timesteps -- this is the "partial"
# optimal transport referenced in the task). Run it independently for each of
# the two consecutive-timestep pairs so the local TimeStep (0/1) that TTK
# reports is unambiguous (0=first frame of the pair, 1=second frame).
pair_grids = []
for i in range(N_STEPS - 1):
    p0 = ps.PassArrays(Input=calcs[i])
    p0.PointDataArrays = ["mag"]
    r0 = ps.Calculator(Input=p0)
    r0.ResultArrayName = "mag_a"
    r0.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    r0.Function = "mag"
    p0b = ps.PassArrays(Input=r0)
    p0b.PointDataArrays = ["mag_a"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p0b)

    p1 = ps.PassArrays(Input=calcs[i + 1])
    p1.PointDataArrays = ["mag"]
    r1 = ps.Calculator(Input=p1)
    r1.ResultArrayName = "mag_b"
    r1.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    r1.Function = "mag"
    p1b = ps.PassArrays(Input=r1)
    p1b.PointDataArrays = ["mag_b"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p1b)

    pair_merged = ps.AppendAttributes(Input=[p0b, p1b])
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=pair_merged)

    tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=pair_merged)
    tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
    tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
    tracking.Timesampling = 1
    tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.15
    tracking.pparameter = "2"
    tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
    tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
    tracking.Xweight = 1.0
    tracking.Yweight = 1.0
    tracking.Zweight = 0.0
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=tracking)

    out = ps.servermanager.Fetch(tracking)
    print(f"pair {i}-{i+1}: N points={out.GetNumberOfPoints()} N cells={out.GetNumberOfCells()}")
    pair_grids.append(out)

# recomputing Z from the LOCAL TimeStep + the pair's starting global index so
# each critical point lands at its correct (x, y, global_time*Z_GAP) location.
all_points = []
all_lines = []
all_ts = []
all_ctype = []
all_pair = []
offset = 0

    pts = ns.vtk_to_numpy(g.GetPoints().GetData())[:, :2]

    global_t = ts_local.astype(float) + i  # pair i covers global steps i, i+1
    z = global_t * Z_GAP
    all_points.append(np.column_stack([pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1], z]))
    all_ts.append(global_t)
    all_ctype.append(ctype)
    all_pair.append(np.full(pts.shape[0], i, dtype=np.int32))
    for c in range(g.GetNumberOfCells()):
        cell = g.GetCell(c)
        ids = [cell.GetPointId(k) + offset for k in range(cell.GetNumberOfPoints())]
        all_lines.append(ids)
    offset += pts.shape[0]

all_pair = np.concatenate(all_pair)

grid.GetPointData().AddArray(ctype_arr)

pair_arr = ns.numpy_to_vtk(all_pair, deep=True)

grid.GetPointData().AddArray(pair_arr)

reassign.GetClientSideObject().SetOutput(grid)

import paraview.simple as ps

N_STEPS = 3
files = [f"/workspace/cylinder/cylinder{i+1}.vti" for i in range(N_STEPS)]

readers = []
calcs = []
for i, fn in enumerate(files):
    r = ps.OpenDataFile(fn)
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=r)
    # combine u,v into a vector array 'vec' (for glyphing) and magnitude scalar (for tracking)
    calc_vec = ps.Calculator(Input=r)
    calc_vec.ResultArrayName = "vec"
    calc_vec.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_vec.Function = "u*iHat+v*jHat"

    calc_mag = ps.Calculator(Input=calc_vec)
    calc_mag.ResultArrayName = f"mag_t{i}"
    calc_mag.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# Keep only the magnitude array (drop u,v,vec) on each branch, then append into one dataset
passers = []
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    p = ps.PassArrays(Input=c)
    p.PointDataArrays = [f"mag_t{i}"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p)
    passers.append(p)

merged = ps.AppendAttributes(Input=passers)
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=merged)

# --- Track critical points across the 3 timesteps using TTK's partial-OT-based
# persistence-diagram matcher (TrackingFromFields: Wasserstein matching allows
# points to be matched to the diagonal, i.e. partial optimal transport between
# consecutive persistence diagrams -- critical points can be born/die between
# steps instead of forcing a full bijection).
tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=merged)
tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
tracking.Timesampling = 1
tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.15
tracking.pparameter = "2"
tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
tracking.Xweight = 1.0
tracking.Yweight = 1.0
tracking.Zweight = 0.0

trackOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(tracking)

print("N points:", trackOut.GetNumberOfPoints(), "N cells:", trackOut.GetNumberOfCells())

# The raw output labels each edge endpoint with a LOCAL TimeStep (0/1) relative
# to its own consecutive-pair match, not a global time index, and edges from
# different (t,t+1) pairs are simply concatenated. Recover the true global
# timestep of every point by nearest-neighbor matching against independently
# computed per-timestep critical point locations, so we can place/color things
# correctly by actual time.
Z_GAP = 180.0


def compute_critical_points(calc_proxy, array_name):
    cp = ps.TTKScalarFieldCriticalPoints(Input=calc_proxy)
    cp.ScalarField = ["POINTS", array_name]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=cp)
    out = ps.servermanager.Fetch(cp)
    import vtk.util.numpy_support as ns
    import numpy as np
    if out.GetNumberOfPoints() == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 2))
    return ns.vtk_to_numpy(out.GetPoints().GetData())[:, :2].astype(float)

    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# --- Track critical points using TTK's partial-OT persistence-diagram matcher
# (TrackingFromFields: sparse-Munkres Wasserstein matching lets a critical
# point be matched to the diagonal, i.e. born/killed, rather than forcing a
# full bijection between consecutive timesteps -- this is the "partial"
# optimal transport referenced in the task). Run it independently for each of
# the two consecutive-timestep pairs so the local TimeStep (0/1) that TTK
# reports is unambiguous (0=first frame of the pair, 1=second frame).
pair_grids = []
for i in range(N_STEPS - 1):
    p0 = ps.PassArrays(Input=calcs[i])
    p0.PointDataArrays = ["mag"]
    r0 = ps.Calculator(Input=p0)
    r0.ResultArrayName = "mag_a"
    r0.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    r0.Function = "mag"
    p0b = ps.PassArrays(Input=r0)
    p0b.PointDataArrays = ["mag_a"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p0b)

    p1 = ps.PassArrays(Input=calcs[i + 1])
    p1.PointDataArrays = ["mag"]
    r1 = ps.Calculator(Input=p1)
    r1.ResultArrayName = "mag_b"
    r1.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    r1.Function = "mag"
    p1b = ps.PassArrays(Input=r1)
    p1b.PointDataArrays = ["mag_b"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p1b)

    pair_merged = ps.AppendAttributes(Input=[p0b, p1b])
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=pair_merged)

    tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=pair_merged)
    tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
    tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
    tracking.Timesampling = 1
    tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.15
    tracking.pparameter = "2"
    tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
    tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
    tracking.Xweight = 1.0
    tracking.Yweight = 1.0
    tracking.Zweight = 0.0
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=tracking)

    out = ps.servermanager.Fetch(tracking)
    print(f"pair {i}-{i+1}: N points={out.GetNumberOfPoints()} N cells={out.GetNumberOfCells()}")
    pair_grids.append(out)

# --- Merge the two pairwise tracking graphs into one vtkUnstructuredGrid,
# recomputing Z from the LOCAL TimeStep + the pair's starting global index so
# each critical point lands at its correct (x, y, global_time*Z_GAP) location.
all_points = []
all_lines = []
all_ts = []
all_ctype = []
all_pair = []
offset = 0
for i, g in enumerate(pair_grids):
    pts = ns.vtk_to_numpy(g.GetPoints().GetData())[:, :2]

grid.SetPoints(vpts)

pair_arr = ns.numpy_to_vtk(all_pair, deep=True)
pair_arr.SetName("PairIndex")
grid.GetPointData().AddArray(pair_arr)

    calc_mag.ResultArrayName = f"mag_t{i}"
    calc_mag.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# one dataset with 3 point-data arrays (one per timestep, in order).
passers = []

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p)

ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=merged)

# persistence-diagram matcher (TrackingFromFields: sparse-Munkres Wasserstein
# matching lets a critical point be matched to the diagonal, i.e. born/killed,
# rather than forcing a full bijection between consecutive timesteps -- this
# is the "partial" optimal transport referenced in the task).
tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=merged)
tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
tracking.Timesampling = 1
tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.15
tracking.pparameter = "2"
tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
tracking.Xweight = 1.0
tracking.Yweight = 1.0
tracking.Zweight = 0.0

    p1b = ps.PassArrays(Input=r1)

import numpy as np
from vtkmodules.util import numpy_support as ns
from vtkmodules.vtkCommonDataModel import vtkUnstructuredGrid
from vtkmodules.vtkCommonCore import vtkPoints

N_STEPS = 3
Z_GAP = 180.0
files = [f"/workspace/cylinder/cylinder{i+1}.vti" for i in range(N_STEPS)]

readers = []
calcs = []
for i, fn in enumerate(files):
    r = ps.OpenDataFile(fn)
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=r)
    # combine u,v into a vector array 'vec' (for glyphing) and magnitude scalar (for tracking)
    calc_vec = ps.Calculator(Input=r)
    calc_vec.ResultArrayName = "vec"
    calc_vec.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_vec.Function = "u*iHat+v*jHat"

    calc_mag = ps.Calculator(Input=calc_vec)
    calc_mag.ResultArrayName = f"mag_t{i}"
    calc_mag.AttributeType = "Point Data"
    calc_mag.Function = "sqrt(u*u+v*v)"

    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=calc_mag)
    readers.append(r)
    calcs.append(calc_mag)

# Keep only the magnitude array (drop u,v,vec) on each branch, then append into
# one dataset with 3 point-data arrays (one per timestep, in order).
passers = []
for i, c in enumerate(calcs):
    p = ps.PassArrays(Input=c)
    p.PointDataArrays = [f"mag_t{i}"]
    ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=p)
    passers.append(p)

merged = ps.AppendAttributes(Input=passers)
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=merged)

# --- Track critical points across the 3 timesteps using TTK's partial-OT
# persistence-diagram matcher (TrackingFromFields: sparse-Munkres Wasserstein
# matching lets a critical point be matched to the diagonal, i.e. born/killed,
# rather than forcing a full bijection between consecutive timesteps -- this
# is the "partial" optimal transport referenced in the task).
tracking = ps.TTKTrackingFromFields(Input=merged)
tracking.Firsttimestep = 0
tracking.Lasttimestep = -1
tracking.Timesampling = 1
tracking.Persistencethreshold = 0.15
tracking.pparameter = "2"
tracking.Extremumweight = 1.0
tracking.Saddleweight = 1.0
tracking.Xweight = 1.0
tracking.Yweight = 1.0
tracking.Zweight = 0.0
ps.UpdatePipeline(time=0, proxy=tracking)

trackOut = ps.servermanager.Fetch(tracking)
print("Tracking output type:", trackOut.GetClassName())
print("N points:", trackOut.GetNumberOfPoints(), "N cells:", trackOut.GetNumberOfCells())

# ConnectedComponentId (a full trajectory chain across all 3 input fields).

# belonging to the same physical location are emitted in temporal sequence as

pts_all = ns.vtk_to_numpy(trackOut.GetPoints().GetData())[:, :2]
cc = ns.vtk_to_numpy(trackOut.GetPointData().GetArray("ConnectedComponentId"))

groups = {}
for idx in range(pts_all.shape[0]):
    groups.setdefault(int(cc[idx]), []).append(idx)

new_points = []
new_lines = []
new_cc = []
new_rank = []
for gid, idxs in groups.items():

rank_arr.SetName("Timestep")
